name: Domain Randomization
summary: Rather than trying to make simulation photorealistic, randomize textures, lighting, camera pose, object properties and physical parameters so widely that the policy must become invariant to them — at which point the real world falls inside the training distribution. This single idea underlies most successful sim-to-real transfer in manipulation.
innovation: Reframed the sim-to-real gap as a generalization problem solvable by variation rather than by fidelity.
Automatic curricula that expand randomization ranges as the policy improves.
matters: The enabling technique behind Dactyl, DeXtreme and most sim-trained dexterity.
limits: Excessive randomization yields conservative, low-performance policies; the ranges need careful tuning.
lineage: The methodological root of sim-to-real transfer.
